reviews.text: All the action, all the emotion, is in Portorosso.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: In Portorosso its inhabitants are against what they call sea monsters. Conversely, the creatures that live under the sea call humans monsters above. So, that world is divided in two microcosms that show that everything depends on the point of view.
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: Director Enrico Casarosa and his team do a magnificent job of bringing small-town Italy to life, interspersed with a coming-of-age fantasy saga.
reviews.author: Gautam Sunder

reviews.text: The animation is painfully generic and even forgettable since its narrative is almost too insignificant.
reviews.author: Diana Tuova

reviews.text: In the end, LUCA is lovely, but slight, and has the potential for so much more. Visually it is gorgeous beyond belief, and... evokes the spiritual transcendence of Studio Ghibli. It doesn’t strive for much more than that, and sometimes that’s fine.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Although this is a Pixar film it is not a Pixar film.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: It was a small, sweet and enjoyable effort from Pixar, which has not only taught us that it's okay to be different from the rest but the importance of it.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: Different than anything PIXAR has done before story wise. Small in scale as A coming of age story that brings the messages of discovery & acceptance!
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: From the detailed animation that makes the Italian coast look realistically astonishing to Dan Romer's rich score that hits all the right notes, without forgetting the outstanding voice work, every Pixar's trademark technical attribute is present.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Pixar made another movie about friendship. But it’s also so much more than that: It’s about how to love life, how to ignore what other people might think of you, and how to accept each other regardless of what or who we really are.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: Even with Luca’s dynamic premise and grand visual splendor, it is not special. Perhaps Pixar’s magic is dimming slowly.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: It's beautiful seeing two kids just be authentically themselves and have fun with each other...
reviews.author: Tyler Strandberg

reviews.text: Luca will be utterly endearing for kids but may be a bit hit and miss for everyone else.
reviews.author: Aaron Phillips

reviews.text: Luca is a charming film with a more relaxed Pixar style that’s made for the dreamers in all of us.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Luca is Pixar at its most emotionally powerful, returning to the resonant storytelling that made the studio such a success to begin with and displaying some of its most arresting animation to date.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Luca conveys the feeling of that who goes to school for the first time and those who see that human-in-the-making going to school for the first time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: "Luca" is pure joy. It's lighter than most Pixar movies, but it's bursting with energy and life. "Luca" will have you smiling from ear to ear.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: LUCA may not have the wow factor of other Pixar films, but in its smaller, lighthearted story it is still so pure and loving that the emotions are really big again in the end.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: A light, enjoyable movie that would look much better coming from any other studio. However, with the weight of history that comes with the Pixar name, many will be expecting more.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: It is a film that is both incredibly charming yet venomous in its emotions that can sneak up on the audience with their power and presence.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Luca is an absolutely charming animated feature that takes audiences to an unforgettably touching trip to Italy.
reviews.author: Mat Brunet

reviews.text: Read on surfaces alone, Luca presents a familiar coming-of-age fable about friendship, albeit impeccably animated and confidently told.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Luca very much wants to be among the big boys, but it cannot find a unique way to go about it.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Luca is a sweet and lighthearted delight that will bring you back to the days of summer vacation and childhood friendship.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: This sweet animation - firmly aimed towards the younger end of the market - is warm and nostalgic as its Fifties Italian setting implies.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: As usual in Pixar films, the characters are well-developed and the story is compelling. The artwork is detailed, bright and colorful. Everything is first-rate. This is a top quality animated film.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The animation is gorgeous - it doesn't hurt that the story takes place on the Italian Riviera - and the attention to detail extends to the background (love the movie posters advertising Roman Holiday and La Strada).
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: It's pleasant watching Luca and Alfonso traipse through the town, but it's so gentle and resistant to excavating anything in real depth, I kept wondering what really it was trying to tell us about friendship or identity.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Even gentler than Pixar's usual fare, 'Luca' is a sweet coming-of-age tale that will leave you wanting to visit the Italian seaside.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: Luca welcomes underdogs and outcasts of all stripes to learn to love themselves, and it encourages us all to look back on our childhoods fondly.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Like one of those summer holidays that you remember fondly but not with any great detail, Luca will happily sit in your mind as a pleasant experience, albeit not one that you'll think about too often.
reviews.author: Rachael Harper

reviews.text: As Pixar's warmest, most preternaturally good-natured films in ages, Luca is an unexpected delight.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: It's a sweet movie, there's no doubt about it... It's not as deep, it's simple, and that's okay.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: A warm and sunny animation which captures the excitement and joy of childhood discovery.
reviews.author: Rob Aldam

reviews.text: Enjoyable enough for an afternoon, but not especially memorable.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: Pixar ditches the grandiloquence of 'Soul' and draws a wonderful straight line to the hearts of the audience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: The movie made me miss my own summertime friendships, with their imperfections and their tenderness, but I couldn't help but feel that the movie, at least by comparison to other Pixar projects, wasn't very ambitious.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: ... Luca is a beautiful, hopeful, and surprisingly deep exploration of change which utilizes the metaphor of physical metamorphosis to explore the philosophical in a tale accessible for the young and young at heart.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Life bubbles up in every corner of Portorosso. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Amador Pérez Andújar

reviews.text: The old "fish out of water" concept takes hold in "Luca," a charming coming-of-age story that uses animation to its fullest.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: Pixar's latest film, Luca, is so chock-full of twists and turns, it reveals just how much that once-little animation studio has helped shape our current "bingeworthy" narrative standard.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Jack Dylan Grazer's voice work is a standout among the cast, but your heart will be taken by the two old Italian ladies who love their gelato.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: A movie about walls coming down and boundaries fading away, with a real sense of limitless potential that will charm young viewers and evoke misty nostalgia in adults.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: A simple story about friendship and self-acceptance that's delightful and a tearjerker. Another strong Pixar entry to its already strong array of films.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Somewhat like a colorful and friendly version of The Creature From the Black Lagoon. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Del Río

reviews.text: Tremendously fun. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: Sea monsters in 1950s Italy. Another high-concept Pixar with aspirational themes. Invitingly colorful and sunny, but still slight, albeit likable, hangout movie for kids.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: If you absolutely need a Pixar movie to scar you emotionally, you'll have to look elsewhere. But that sort of thing doesn't matter to kids, who along with their parents can just kick back and enjoy Luca as the warm-hearted, splashy summer fun it is.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: You don't need to have a love for Italian food or music to appreciate the charming story in Luca, but a little gelato will make it even sweeter.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: A magical fable about the power of friendship and allyship needed to build a more inclusive and empathetic world. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Families will be wrapped around their TV sets, having a good time together with this...
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: It is a beautifully done animation with captivating characters and profound and resonant themes. Luca is still an enjoyable summer flick about adolescence and independence.
reviews.author: Tatat Bunnag

reviews.text: 'Luca' is a splash of Italian adventure.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: In a heatwave of heavy subject matter, Luca's light and breezy story is a welcoming reprieve.
reviews.author: Alicia Gilstorf

reviews.text: Change starts with one person, Luca posits, and it can destroy power structures, foster acceptance, and bring everyone together. In an increasingly isolated world, that's a great message.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: Arriving just before the first official day of summer, Luca embodies the spirit of the season.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Apart from more dramatic and tragic Pixar films, Luca is a smaller story about friendship and identity.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Outside of these small peaks, though, the movie simply doesn't hit emotionally as it ought to, conveying close connection.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: It's full of energy and the diligence of those researchers has paid off in its settings which are seductive -- and even more important -- believable.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Yes, Luca owes a debt to numerous other films, but it still manages to stand on its own two flippers and exist as a reasonably unique, and entirely enjoyable, thing.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Feels like a good fit for what used to be direct-to-video.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: The film treads water amid a sea of animated tropes.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: Luca is unspeakably lovely, incredibly charming and a celebration of being yourself with the people who matter most and finding the good ones in life.
reviews.author: Jack Bottomley

reviews.text: May not quite be top-tier Pixar, but it is certainly top-tier meaningful.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Absolutely delightful.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: "Luca" is good because of its simplicity.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Luca is a sweet, gentle, sun-kissed film, with gentle rhythms and a generous spirit.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: This buoyantly engaging Pixar tale directed by Enrico Casarosa, the maker of the Oscar-nominated 2011 short La Luna, provides enough catchy hooks to please most family viewers.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: Luca has enough going for it that it can overcome a script that is more on the shallow end of the pool. This is more about the mood and look of the film, which is bright and interesting and full of life.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Pixar reels you in with another delightful bait of a movie, and you can't help but fall for it hook, line and sinker. Sure to warm the heart of even the coldest fish is Luca's tale of a summer bromance on the Italian seaside.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: A tender, playful bop that revels in the small stuff while still delivering the emotional resonance that's become its studio's signature.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: A simple but effective coming of age story from Pixar. It may not swing for the fences, but the characters and their friendship are charming.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: A colourful story about friendship, this animated feature revels in Pixar's ability to combine comically engaging storytelling with deeper thematic resonance.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Luca is a colorful summer romp that examines the importance of family, friendship and a good bowl of pasta. Its message of hope comes at a time when we can appreciate it the most.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: There is more going on in this charming variation on a fish-out-of-water story that has obstacles, dangers, friendships, understanding others and, above all, love for one another.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: A vibrant, charming story of friendship with gorgeous visuals of the Italian Riviera. But I'd say this one is 'Pixar lite' as it lacks the depth + emotional resonance I expect from the studio.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: The real winners are the young moviegoers who will learn that Luca respects and cares about them enough to challenge them while also delivering a good time.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Luca is also a lot lighter than the kinds of highly-emotive films Pixar has become known for, instead trading in simple pleasures and child-like wonder.
reviews.author: Kate Robertson

reviews.text: It works well as an entertaining family experience, with an admirable message of inclusion and tolerance, and a very high quality of animation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: While the big theme is not as in-your-face compared with other recent Pixar films, Luca still packs in the right amount of charm, character and heart for this fish-out-of-water tale of friendship and finding your path.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: Luca is a continual delight, a film that will make you feel warm, fuzzy and wanting for more. The film's length of 96 minutes - considerable for a Pixar feature - feels transitory, because you want this vicarious visit to coastal Italy to go on and on.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: The most Ghibli thing that Pixar has done so far. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: Luca is packed with technical brilliance... full of vitality and joie de vivre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: A pleasant, snoozy kids' movie.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Does this film reach the heights of Pixar's greatest films? No. No one is going to put this one in the pantheon. However, it is a gentle and gently entertaining reminder that even second- or third-tier Pixar means a high-quality movie experience.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: This movie takes joy in the everyday things...wonderful moments.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: It's as sweet and refreshing as that first dip in the sea on a hot summer's day: you might have done it last year, but the tingle on your skin and the heady rush of adrenaline never loses its shine.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: ...the film's kindness, enthusiasm, and big heart will win over most audiences and stand up to plenty of repeated viewings on the Disney+ platform.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: A slight, slow-burning story that eventually blossoms into a beautiful, crowdpleasing tale, Luca might be a lesser entry in the Pixar pantheon, but it still contains plenty of delights and memorable moments.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Luca is a sincere, wonderfully imagined fable.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: A real mood lifter with important themes!
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: An exciting fish out of water adventure - literally - that's perfect for the summer.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: This isn't just a coming-of-age story. It's also a story of learning and exploring friendship. An epic adventure. This is a summer flick you want to take your family to see.
reviews.author: Wendy Lee Szany

reviews.text: Luca has all the zip and ingenuity, all right.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Hardly top-tier Pixar, but offers stunning production design, talented voice actors and a message so sweet, you'd have to be looking to find anything wrong with it.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Luca, basically, is great news for film nerds and wonder-starved kids.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: While it's a little disappointing to hear that any queerness viewers see in Luca is unofficial & subtext, it's not stopping the impact a film like this can have on young queer kids who can grow up and see a little bit of themselves represented on screen.
reviews.author: Raffy Ermac

reviews.text: In the nuts and bolts of its storytelling, and its low-stakes charm, Luca may well be the best kid-focused Pixar tale since Coco.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Less ambitious than most of the studio's films, "Luca" instead projects plenty of warmth, specifically in its study of identity, bigotry and the challenges young people face when navigating their anxiety-inducing entry into adulthood.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: I struggled to find what was unusual or recommendable for this one... It is B-list Pixar.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: It is lesser Pixar, but lesser Pixar is still better than a lot of other animation.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: While I give [Pixar] points for trying things a little simpler and making some of the animation a little more cartoony in places, it's very talky [and] very familiar.
reviews.author: Charles Solomon

reviews.text: It rarely reaches the heights of other Pixar gems, but the clever melding of surf and turf entices with its own share of pleasures; each lure so colorful and scrumptious, you swallow it hook, line and sinker.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: It overcomes a tide of stumbling blocks, even as it makes crystal clear a need for the training wheels to come off when it comes to LGBTQ+ representation. Enough baby steps, Pixar folks.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Casarosa's film makes a virtue of being simple and unchallenging. Despite the mortal peril in which the lead characters spend half of the movie, the overall mood is light and larkish rather than tense.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: A summer vacation in one's living room, it will leave you smiling from gill to gill.
reviews.author: Stephen Humphries

reviews.text: It's adorable and airy, just like the picturesque coastal village where the movie takes place.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: While Luca will probably not go down as one of the top classics in the Pixar canon because it lacks the conceptual genius of something like Up or Inside Out, it is nevertheless the most purely endearing original film that they have done in a while.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Luca may not feel as revolutionary as some of Pixar's finest films, but it feels familiar in the best possible way; like revisiting fond memories of glorious childhood summers.
reviews.author: Phil W. Bayles

reviews.text: As long as you don't come in hoping for anything too groundbreaking, you're likely to love this movie, whether it's for yourself or the kids in your life. Funny, heartwarming, and beautiful, it's a highlight of the summer.
reviews.author: Caitlin Wyneken

reviews.text: Harmless, safe, kid-centric entertainment that barely feels like a Pixar production.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Not every movie has to be a masterpiece, but for a studio that has produced so many of them, this feels like a lower tier entry.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: There is some whimsical charm in all this but the whimsy too often feels forced, the characters don't engage enough and the animation rarely reaches Pixar's usual stratospheric heights or, indeed, underwater depths...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: While director Enrico Casarosa has made a beautiful, pastel-tinted film about friendship and adventure in Luca, it is never thought-provokingly powerful like other great Pixar films.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: From any other company, "Luca" would be underwhelming and easily forgettable. Coming from Pixar, however, long the gold standard in animation, it's a disappointment, another sign the studio's stamp is not what it once was. Toss this one back in the water.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: It's a heartwarming story about friendship, stepping out of your comfort zone and two teenage sea monsters who experience a life-changing summer.
reviews.author: John Byrne

reviews.text: For those who accuse Pixar of overthinking it with some of their films: you're definitely not going to say that of Luca.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: That's a love story worth telling to all ages.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: The heart of the film, the friendship, and relationship between Luca and Alberto, is so meticulously felt and realized that everything around it, all the flights of fancy and mustachioed boat-cats, ride with peachy ease in its wake.
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: The standard of the company's earlier works is so high and their reputation so glowing that 'reasonably good' seems a comparative indictment.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: While Luca might lack some of the dizzying inventiveness that marks out top-tier Pixar, it's packed to the gills with charm.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: "Luca" has messages of accepting others' differences and breaking down barriers. I loved all the humor, the magical and brightly colored scenes, and the energetic musical score.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Even though all of the subplots are interconnected and flow into one another, it still feels a bit crowded thematically.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: An excellent summer family film, Disney Pixar's "Luca" will enchant parents and children alike.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Luca is a winning movie on many levels and works best as a vibrant story about the pure joys of childhood adventure and imagination.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The story's bright swirl of Pixar pixie dust, jangle soundtrack, and gentle lessons on accepting otherness and learning to move past fear feel like a temporary passport: a sweetly soulful all-ages dip in la dolce vita.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: It's generic and ordinary and, although it contains sufficient material to engage children, its ability to hold the attention of older viewers is less sure.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Pixar's remarkably absorbing "Luca" is a legitimate fish out of water tale with an abundance of "Pinocchio" overtones.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: It wont' break any Pixar ground like Finding Nemo or Inside Out, but it's a sweet fable that kids will like.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: "Luca" is a minor charmer.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: A love letter to the summers of youth, Luca is a heartwarming and adventurous story about friendship, acceptance, and celebrating the underdog.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: A refreshing, lovely story of adventure, friendship & acceptance, set against the beautiful Italian culture and landscape. A great family flick for the summer. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: A sweet animated film that finds its place celebrating the wonder of simple lives.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: It's gorgeous, and it's sweet, and it's charming, and it's funny. It's everything you want from a Pixar movie.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: It also gets fine mileage from a recurring "Looney Tunes"-style joke: the monster friends must avoid getting wet, which causes their scales to inconveniently re-appear.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: With vibrant visuals, an amazing voice cast and important messages, Luca solidifies itself as one of DisneyPixar's best.
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: From the bright colors, the landscape, the food, the little Italian phrases nestled in the dialogue, the cultural identity of the Italian people was acknowledged and actualized.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: Luca is a delicate animated fantasy that seems afraid of its own metaphors.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: You may not walk away from it pondering the nature of the soul. But maybe you'll look up at a tree's branches swaying in the wind, or turn your face up to the sun for a minute...
reviews.author: Melissa Leon

reviews.text: The rich personal touches in Luca are elevated by Pixar's signature clever humor, sharp storytelling, and watchable scenery.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Playful and beautifully-animated, this may be the most easily-digestible Pixar movie ever.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: A modest entry in the Pixar canon, with a script that lacks the depth and thematic complexity of some of its predecessors, this breezy coming-of-age adventure still has charm to spare.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The best way to sum up the film is as a mash-up of Kiki's Delivery Service and Wolf Children.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Following Pixar's many high-achieving movies, "Luca" underachieves, its best moments negated by lengthy stretches of mediocrity.
reviews.author: John Wirt

reviews.text: Pixar has such a strong track record as a studio that no one will begrudge it the rare miss. After Soul, it was fair to wonder how Pixar would top the Oscar winner. Well, it didn't.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Enrico Casarosa of the Oscar nominated short animation "La Luna," makes his feature debut with this charming fish-out-of-water tale that celebrates acceptance along with all things peculiar to the Italian Riviera.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: I could watch these two boys enjoying their time together, making a scooter, for the rest of my life, and I hope that kids love Luca as much as I did.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: Luca delivers a slice of one so rich and sweet, you'll practically taste the gelato on your lips for hours afterward. It's a simple pleasure, and one sure to make you smile.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: More significantly, the musical elements are reduced, though what is played as counterpoint to the action is infectious. Search YouTube for the soundtrack - the bouncy retro Italo pop is irresistible.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: If ever there was a film to triumph moving from one medium to another, it's this ocean-to-land fairytale.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: What Luca most conspicuously lacks is Pixar's penchant for throwing up a big tent for all ages. There's less for grown-ups in the studio's youngest-skewing effort since the Cars franchise.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: That darkness is tantalizing - a toe dip into subversive waters - but the filmmakers remain stubbornly incurious.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: Casarosa's film comes and goes like a soft summer breeze, but that doesn't stop it from being utterly charming.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: Luca is an enjoyably featherweight film that aims to be little more than a fanciful diversion - and maybe is all the better for it.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Lucadoesn't look or sound like any film Pixar has made before. It has a charm all its own and captures our imagination from the moment it begins. I found myself on the verge of tears in the closing moments of this wonderful, disarming film.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: There is pasta and gelato, fountains and cycling, a mustache-twirling villain and starry night skies. It's a tiny vacation with a healthy serving of imagination.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: While Luca is Pixar's 24th animated feature, it might be the first one that is properly called a cartoon.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: "Luca" is a charming coming-of-age story with some Italian seasoning that should serve up a good time for the whole family.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: If you've ever wondered what it would be like if someone combined The Little Mermaid and Call Me By Your Name, look no further.
reviews.author: Kevin Brackett

reviews.text: Luca will fill a gap for less-demanding younger viewers. It's well-meaning. It's lively. It's moderately funny. But it is no Finding Nemo.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: It's a simple but rewarding message well-told via a small scale story. Pixar's choice not to go too deep on this one simply allows the film to be what it wants to be.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: We wanted more from this film to cheer "long live Luca," but at best, Luca is a pleasant fish-out-of-water story.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: A Mondo Italiano Little Mermaid that embraces its Mediterranean archetypes with a that's-ah-spicy-meat-ah-ball fervor-and it still breaks your heart.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: A story simply about a couple of friends in the Mediterranean for the summer could have been unbelievable and fantastical as-is. I didn't see the need to add the supernatural element to something that already is dreamy and almost filled with magic.
reviews.author: Patricia Puentes

reviews.text: The simple, understated beauty of "Luca" may relegate it to "minor" Pixar status. But I'd take minor Pixar over almost anything else, and the lovely, wistful delights of "Luca" are refreshing to plunge into.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Like all modern Pixar films, there is a deep beauty in the animation, and an emphasis on story that expresses all that beauty and in this case, humor. It also Hearts FELLINI!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Pixar's latest animated adventure has friendship at its core, delivering the feel-good movie of the summer that will warm your heart with its enveloping rays of lighthearted fun.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: Celebrate age 13 with 'Luca', a pleasant Pixar journey.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: It's not in the same league as such Pixar classics as 'WALL-E' and 'Toy Story,' but there's no denying the pure enchantment of the visual, comic and subtextual dazzle in this tale of two sea monsters trying to pass for human boys in 1960's Italy.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The film creates impeccable splendor for the eyes and heart.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: The film does a good job delving into the power of friendship and self-discovery between Luca and Alberto.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Young kids will eat up this film like a freshly dipped biscotti, but adults will be left with a rather disappointing aftertaste.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: An affectionate portrait of friendship that never quite rises to the level of Pixar's best efforts.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: The moral wins no points for originality, but is handled by Pixar with typical sophistication and nuance...
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: There is... just enough atmospheric detail and, in the final lap, enough genuine feeling in the thorny friendships to make it worth seeing.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: A mildly entertaining, harmless diversion that panders, mostly, to young audiences without the sophistication found in far better Pixar films about friendship like Ratatouille.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: It's unquestionably fun, but not much more.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: LUCA is about acceptance and not judging someone by their appearance -- like the color of their skin, er scales.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: [I]ts pleasures are slight and fleeting.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: This gem of a film features a really good story that even young children will follow -- yet it is still entertaining for adults.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Pixar typically creates full and robust animation with fleshed-out characters and bright and bold hues. Luca is no different in this regard.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Paper thin for Pixar, and totally at home on Disney Plus instead of theaters. But it's a beautiful film that captures the magic of the coast of Italy, and has a strong ending.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: I'm not seeing this leaving a lasting impact like most of Pixar's movies.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: With a sweet and simple tale of friendship brought to life by stunning animation, Luca is a joyful adventure for the whole family
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: I don't expect Pixar to hit a home run every time, but I do expect more than the single they deliver with Luca.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: A beautiful fable about the things that life gives us, takes from us, and some others that we have to say "Silenzio Bruno!", and dare to reach for. Immensely recommended! [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: It's clearly a labor of love, and a pictorial feast containing intricate tributes and touching homages... [But] as pleasing as the film is, some of it feels arbitrary, underdeveloped, possibly rushed.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: As far as warm-weather comfort movies go, it's hard to get one more satisfying than this.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: In less subtle hands the messages of respect, loyalty and decency might have a preachy tone, but Pixar never condescends to its audience, and proves once again a mastery of moral storytelling wrapped in mirth.
reviews.author: Terry Staunton

reviews.text: While Luca is far from a failure, there's nothing especially memorable about it, either. It's great that the studio is trying something different instead of relying on its go-to properties, but in this instance, the impact just isn't there.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: "Luca" keeps it light, which is not necessarily a bad thing. The latest from Pixar is as bright, refreshing and instantly forgettable as an Italian ice.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: While it's not bad, the movie ultimately feels like a little fish in a big pond.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Instead of just adorable, Luca comes frustratingly close to being precise instead of wandering, decisive instead of dithering, substantial instead of cute, fluffy and trivial.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: Despite [its] rather pedestrian approach to plotting, the heart and soul of Luca make it shine.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: It's about the sometimes risky discovery of pleasure, and it's a pleasure to discover.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: A sweet story of friendship with a gorgeous 50s/60s Italian setting, some spectacular underwater animation and a sprinkling of memorable supporting characters. It remains to be seen if this is the start of an upward swing for Pixar.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: As with any Pixar film, the visuals in Luca are stunning, awash in vibrant colors and the warm sunlit tones of summer. There's charm and humor for days, and the supporting characters are delightful.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: It may not have the belly laughs or excitement of a Finding Nemo or Toy Story... but it is nonetheless a delightful and likeable film.
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: Luca doesn't have the emotional resonance of classic era Pixar but what it lacks in gut punch sentiment, it makes up for in imagination, action and the good-natured look at finding a place to belong, above and below sea level.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Sometimes comfort food is the best food because it reminds you of your childhood. It reminds you of home. Luca is Pixar comfort food.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: Pixar's reliably lovely computer-animated latest might be lacking in the magic of their finest hours but, admittedly, they've set the bar incredibly high for themselves.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: A hugely pleasurable film to spend time with; at times, it's as rejuvenating as luxuriating in the Mediterranean sunshine.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: The fact that it's a film that celebrates someone's differences is more than enough to deem Luca beyond a second-tier title.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Unlike Soul, and so many other recent Pixar films, Luca isn't aiming for photorealism; it's the rare cartoon movie that looks and feels like a cartoon movie.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: It follows an time-honored path to an ending that will warm the cockles of your cardiac organ while also making you question the best way to eat pasta.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Luca is such a wonderful film that could be watched over and over again. Full of joy and wonder with a great story and theme of connection and becoming.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Though it's not as psychologically ambitious as some of the studio's other films, Pixar delivers an absolute charmer in this sweet animated fable about unlikely friendships and the acceptance of the differences among us.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: While relatively tame and simplistic as far as Pixar concepts go, there's more than enough charm and vivacity in Luca to make for a sweet, lighthearted summer flick.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Proves that nurturing an open mindset is a good way to foster a better today and tomorrow.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Sweetly splashy and whimsical, it's Pixar's family-friendly fare.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: It's maybe not in the same vaulted league of such classic Pixar toons... but its latest, Luca, is the best excuse ever to escape the summertime heat and treat yourself to this lilting and entertaining sea monster coming-of-age charmer.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: For the most part... "Luca" is light and effervescent as a summertime Bellini, which is something parents can drink while the kids watch this.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Despite its [familiarity], 'Luca' is a deliciously adorable tale with lovable characters, dazzling visuals and colors, and a tender message about growing up that hits you square in the heart.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Sure, it doesn't rival Pixar's best, but I silence any doubters by quoting Luca's mantra: "Silencio, Bruno!"
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Skip this and get your kids to watch a Fellini movie instead.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: This heartfelt, gorgeously animated adventure is a short and sweet reminder of sun-filled summer days with new friends.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: Fast-paced and full of color and light, Luca takes a more probing look at pubescent friendships than we expect from a piece of animated entertainment.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: What it does have are some groovy Italian pop songs and a setting as pleasant as a summer afternoon. The light glimmers off the surface of the ocean without any worry of going too deep.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: A gentle, overtly Miyazaki-esque coming-of-age period piece struggles under the heavy weight of iron-clad Disney/Pixar formula requirements and story beats.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: Italian shores, pasta and sea monsters make for an enjoyable animated summer tale of friendship reminding audiences of those childhood friendships that shape who we ultimately become
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: a major disappointment, because its vitally important themes about pride and identity are all but lost, wrapped up in a movie that itself doesn't really know what it wants to be.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: If I know America like I think I know America, too much discussion about the film's universal themes will get derailed by claims and counterclaims about what it is "really" about.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: A super fun summer hangout film that prioritises friendship over spectacle.
reviews.author: Liam Maguren

reviews.text: Luca is a delightful tale of summer friendship the whole family will love
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: A delightful coming-of-age adventure with a beautifully subtle and poignant examination of hiding who you really are to fit in.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: As you get immersed in the story, you're also entranced by a lovely escape to a nostalgic Italian summer that's inspired by visits to real-life places and rendered in a style akin to that distinctive Miyazaki aesthetic.
reviews.author: Aparita Bhandari

reviews.text: Just like Luca and Alberto are one thing on land and another when submerged, Casarosa's Luca is at once a bright ray of sunshine and a deep dive into fraternal connection.
reviews.author: Carlos Aguilar

reviews.text: Watching it is like relaxing in the sunshine.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: There's nothing not to like about Luca, really, but it's worth considering that even the least of Miyazaki's films are more than just a pretty face.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Luca, the debut feature from long-term Pixar artist Enrico Casarosa, is perhaps more derivative than we've come to expect from the studio (narratively speaking, it can sometimes feel a little underdeveloped too). But it's still pretty charming...
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Luca is an endearing, but predictable tale of two teenage sea monsters; who pose as human boys and discover "la dolce vita" in Italy.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Pixar has made so many great movies that when they make one that's merely good, it almost feels like a disappointment. Case in point: Luca.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: While one could argue that 'Luca' is simply a story about accepting outsiders, the subtext of a homosexual love story gives the film its spark.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: 'Luca' ... is a splash of fresh air, a feature that reminds us that despite outward appearances, we all are the same inside.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Luca tries to stand for too many things without having the sea legs to support them.
reviews.author: B.L. Panther

reviews.text: I don't need a cry-your-eyes-out Pixar movie every time. Luca is beautiful and a feel-good family movie for the summer.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: The plot may follow familiar pathways towards resolution with well-worn themes, but the ways in which it finds those in-roads are often subtle and poignant.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It's a story about identity as much as it is a well-written and gorgeously rendered tale of misfit friendship. People of all ages will likely find the film a source of strength
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: It's strange to write that a kids story is about a pair of sea monsters, living in their own underwater universe, but everything about Luca works, in a delightful story about conquering fears and new friendships.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Another one of Pixar's wondrous and warm creations; a fantastical tale that's deeply rooted in human emotion and quandary.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Luca, as with most Pixar movies, is gorgeously animated, combining gently stylized humans with splendidly realistic environments.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: A great slice-of-life that is a love letter to Italy, summer, and the life-long bonds we make during the season.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Casarosa's visually stunning coming-of-age film is a heartfelt ode to childhood, friendship, and self-discovery.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: It's as sweet and breezy as a scoop of gelato and who doesn't like gelato?
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: This movie may not make you cry but for sure it will make you sigh in appreciation. And it has a spit take for the ages.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: How do you know you're watching a Pixar movie, besides the great visuals? The lead characters are usually male and struggling with identity/self-esteem issues ... and they find out the meaning of life with some tearjerking moments. The End.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Far from Pixar's best, "Luca" still delivers visual splendor
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: An airy story of summer friendship on the Italian Rivera.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Luca is an Italian getaway you should take when it's available, even when it will all-too-quickly become a haze once it's over.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: "Luca" is lovely, just not in a sustained way Pixar is occasionally capable of delivering.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Authentic, personal and surprisingly low stakes.
reviews.author: Kambole Campbell

reviews.text: A simple (perhaps overly so, especially for a Pixar piece) yet pleasant little fable.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The film is lovely and funny, but it operates on a more minor key than some of Pixar's true classics.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Luca is a visually stunning film with a powerful message about friendship, acceptance, and squashing prejudices. A joy to watch.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: This movie will fill your heart up. Enrico Casarosa is an artist with a true perspective, fearless in his creative impulses and limitless in his compassion, and "Luca" is a pure expression of these sensibilities.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: Luca sets a very particular mood, and it's one that fits right in with a warm summer night.
reviews.author: Andrew Webster

reviews.text: Pixar's high standards of storytelling and animation are on full display, but what's refreshing about "Luca" is that it doesn't yank on the tear ducts like some Pixar titles have done.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Luca plays an enjoyable coming-of-age story with one foot in the water and the other placed in fantasy.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Sometimes a simple story is all you need to make a perfect film. Pixar doesn't need to make you question your life to craft a great time
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: "A minor, kid-facing diversion that scans like a waste of time from such a talented animation powerhouse."
reviews.author: Steven Warner

reviews.text: This is a film filled to the brim with joy and wonder, leaving you smiling hours after you watch it, feeling once again like a kid on the first day of summer.
reviews.author: Charlie Ridgely

reviews.text: Luca is a different adventure from Disney-Pixar but it's still a heartwarming tale.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: It may not be a masterpiece, but its message is one that can't be expressed enough. "Luca" expresses it in a gorgeous, fun way.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: The target audience will likely be at an advantage over their parents... because the younger you are, the better the chances you won't notice glaring similarities to The Little Mermaid.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Luca is a simpler, lighter movie from Pixar. It's funny, warm, and reminds us that we're all worth far more than our darker moments sometimes suggest.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: The layered dynamics and pure, honest emotions underneath Luca's simple coming-of-age story are what elevate the film to one of Pixar's best.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: [Luca] offers the studio's hallmark visual splendor, yet fails to venture outside of safe waters.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: There are worse things a family summer movie can be than sweet, kind, and affirming of interspecies friendship in all its forms.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: LUCA presents an overly predictable, yet classic story. However, the animation is gold, capturing the feel of the sea as well as the character of the Italian Riveria.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: All in all, Luca is very good. It's just missing a certain cohesiveness that would've made it great.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: 'Luca' is a small-scale and charming kid-friendly adventure from a time before Pixar films were expected to be monumental deconstructions of life's biggest questions.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: "Luca" is middle-drawer Pixar, a dreamily animated bit of whimsy with a great setting, not much of a story, and a concept that's a rehash.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Something of a companion piece to the superior Finding Nemo, this is one of Pixar's weaker efforts but still worth catching.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: Sweet and affecting, capturing the bond that strangers can build over a summer, and how that friendship can endure. And like its shape-shifting protagonists, it's got plenty going on beneath the surface.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: It doesn't have the emotional resonance of the studio's best work, and definitely won't have the shelf life either - but while watching, many will find themselves won over by the effectiveness of its fairytale simplicity.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Struggles to dog-paddle to avoid sinking amid the ocean of expectations that come along with the Pixar brand.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: "Luca," like its charming village at low tide, is a shallow dip in the water.
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: Director Enrico Casarosa is making his feature-length debut here, and he and the vast Pixar animation army have delivered a gorgeous and lovely coming-of-age fantasy...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: One of Pixar's smaller, sweeter efforts...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: LUCA is a sweet and beautifully animated movie for everyone. Alberto and Luca make for an entertaining duo with wonderful chemistry.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: "Luca" doesn't drown in the usual Pixar profundity yet still navigates coming-of-age themes quite swimmingly with some appealing animated youngsters.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: When it comes to Luca, they [Pixar] certainly found a refreshing way to do it again.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Another reliably slick combination of the Pixar playbook elements we've come to know so well, it's a gentle, calming whisper that grows faint once it's over.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: It's a visually beguiling small-town nostalgia trip, as well as a perfectly pleasant fish-out-of-water fable - literally, since it's about a boy sea monster who longs to go ashore.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: There's fun to be had with Luca, but heaps of colour aren't enough to disguise an uninspired animation style and story that make it feel like Pixar is treading water in the wake of much better movies like Coco and Onward.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: "Luca" is big in all the ways that count; it's the screens that got small.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Something cute and slightly indistinct and on Pixar model: a tropical blur of minor whimsy and carpe diem platitude.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: The Genoa native's obvious deep-rooted affection for life in simpler times on Italy's northwest coast gives the movie a warming injection of real heart.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: With Luca, Pixar recaptures a lot of the magic and heart that its animations are known for while providing a lovely, heartwarming character journey.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: A strange hybrid of Italian neorealism and fish-based fantasy, Luca is beautiful to behold but plays it too safe to make a real impact. Still, great CG linguine.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: Luca is a gorgeous, tender-hearted paean to childhood summers spent with sunburnt noses and callused fingers, and to the friendships that have helped us discover who we are.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The script, with all of its wit and perfectly interwoven story threads and running gags, bears all the hallmarks of the best of Pixar's story trust.
reviews.author: Brian Roan

reviews.text: But mostly the message is more universal the tearjerking finale is as authentic as ever, and the film is ultimate proof, if it was needed, that Pixar remains the inviolable master of cinema soul food for kids of all ages.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Pixar's Luca may not be one of the animation studio's strongest efforts, but it's still a sweet summer getaway.
reviews.author: Nicole Clark

reviews.text: It may not be the best Pixar movie, or the riskiest - it sure as hell isn't the most ambitious - but "Luca" is also one of the precious few that feels like it isn't afraid to be something else.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Luca is one of the brightest films Pixar has ever made. A happy place to escape this summer. A movie filled with adventure, comedy and heart. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jesus Agudo

reviews.text: Luca will please children and parents alike. The message of friendship is a strong one, the visuals are lush, and you're going to want pasta when it's all over.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Pixar's most intimate and laidback effort since Ratatouille feels like a throwback to one of Mark Twain's rollicking picaresque sagas.
reviews.author: Keith Watson

reviews.text: A sweet, vibrant charmer of a film that serves as a beautiful ode to young friendship.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Audiovisual joy for all ages... [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: The last fifteen minutes of Luca might go down as one of the best endings Pixar has ever produced.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: Luca's story of friendship might be simple, but it's effectively done and told with a lot of heart. You'll laugh, you'll cry and you'll wish Portorosso was real.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: Luca hasn't quite got his sea legs, but is a sweet enough story for a summer family flick.
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: A gorgeously life-affirming cinematic adventure with stunning imagination and a totally heartwarming exploration of friendship... It's loaded with important messages and packs an incredibly powerful punch. Bright, lively and exciting.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: Luca is hugely enjoyable, beautifully animated, and very sweet. Disney Pixar has most definitely still got it.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: Maybe not every Pixar movie can be "Up." For now, we'll just let adorable be enough.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

synopsis: Set in a beautiful seaside town on the Italian Riviera, Disney and Pixar's original feature film "Luca" is a coming-of-age story about one young boy experiencing an unforgettable summer filled with gelato, pasta and endless scooter rides. Luca (voice of Jacob Tremblay) shares these adventures with his newfound best friend, Alberto (voice of Jack Dylan Grazer), but all the fun is threatened by a deeply-held secret: they are sea monsters from another world just below the water's surface.
